title: Adding, Updating, and Removing Hash Entries
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of adding, updating, and removing hash entries in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.

content.intro: Learn Adding, Updating, and Removing Hash Entries through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding adding, updating, and removing hash entries helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Adding, Updating, and Removing Hash Entries helps you reason about inserting and replacing entries. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Inserting and replacing entries. Then connect it to delete. The remaining syllabus points—merge, Collision behavior during merging—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.
